key_insight: The paper introduces a high-order finite-difference framework that preserves relativistic physical constraints by converting nonlinear admissibility conditions into solvable linearized limiting problems.
engineering_relevance: It enables robust, shock-resolving special relativistic hydrodynamics simulations without numerical breakdown near strong discontinuities, even in multiple dimensions.
method: Uses a GQL reformulation to turn positivity and subluminal-velocity constraints into families of linear inequalities.
Embeds a Zalesak-type flux-corrected transport limiter into finite-difference WENO updates on conservative variables.
Computes optimal limiter parameters non-iteratively via small eigenvalue problems using a stereographic parameterization.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports extensive 1D–3D benchmarks, including ultra-relativistic Riemann problems and astrophysical jets, showing stability, discontinuity resolution, and design-order accuracy on smooth flows.
watch_item: The multidimensional limiter still relies on solving small eigenproblems and relaxed variants, so implementation cost and robustness of parameter selection need careful attention in large-scale 3D runs.
paper_title: GQL-Based Physical-Constraint-Preserving High-Order Finite Difference Schemes for Special Relativistic Hydrodynamics in Arbitrary Dimensions
